import pandas as pd

# File paths for source data
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/test_1.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Schema: ['userId', 'movieId', 'tag', 'timestamp']
source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Schema: ['movieId', 'title', 'genres']

# Inspect schemas:
# source0: userId, movieId, tag, timestamp
# source1: movieId, title, genres
# Target schema: ['movieId', 'title', 'genres', 'userId', 'tag', 'timestamp']

# Join source0 and source1 on 'movieId' to get all columns for the target
# source0 has userId, tag, timestamp; source1 has title, genres
# Join type: inner join on movieId to keep only matching movieIds (consistent with target examples)

merged = pd.merge(source0, source1, on='movieId', how='inner')

# Reorder columns to match target schema
target_columns = ['movieId', 'title', 'genres', 'userId', 'tag', 'timestamp']
result = merged[target_columns]

# Ensure correct dtypes according to target schema:
# movieId: integer
result['movieId'] = result['movieId'].astype(int)
# title: string (object)
result['title'] = result['title'].astype(str)
# genres: string (object)
result['genres'] = result['genres'].astype(str)
# userId: integer
result['userId'] = result['userId'].astype(int)
# tag: string (object)
result['tag'] = result['tag'].astype(str)
# timestamp: integer
result['timestamp'] = result['timestamp'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/target_multisource_cot.csv"
result.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
